edge.title: The helpful man at the branch
edge.setup: A branch executive you have known for years says there is a better return than your FD, a special scheme that is not on the website. Hand over the cheque or cash today, he will 'process it internally' and give you a handwritten acknowledgement. He is in uniform, at his desk, inside the bank.
edge.tell: Your money leaves your hands, but no entry appears under your name in your own bank app or statement.
move: Pay only by transfer from your own account to a product you can see in your own app or on a system-generated receipt.
Never hand cash or a cheque to an individual, whatever the building he sits in.
Check your statement and SMS the same day; if the entry is missing, escalate in writing to the branch manager and the bank's grievance channel.
edge.why: A familiar face and a bank's walls stand in for verification, but only your own record of the transaction proves where the money went. A side deal is built to live outside that record, so it cannot be seen, insured or reversed. The check works on any scheme, whoever is offering it.
edge.variants: Same shape: the agent who 'invests' premiums himself, the society treasurer who holds the corpus in his own account, the relative who 'pools' money for a chit.

lens.name: Principal–agent problem
lens.one_line: The person acting for you is paid for something subtly different from what you want.
lens.detail: A broker is paid when a deal closes, not when you choose well. An insurance agent is paid on commission, which differs by product. A contractor is paid for the job, not for the job lasting. None of this requires bad intent — the incentive is enough. Knowing the pay structure predicts the advice better than knowing the person.
elsewhere: Fund managers judged quarterly take risks that look fine quarterly.
A politician's horizon is the next election; infrastructure's horizon is thirty years.
A mechanic paid per part replaced finds more parts to replace.
lens.test: Before weighing advice, ask: what exactly triggers this person getting paid?
lens.today: Fresh bids for Bengaluru's garbage collection contracts have undercut the earlier rates, and Bengaluru Solid Waste Management Ltd is defending the original contracts (The Times of India). Whoever signs a contract is paid by the terms of the contract, not by how clean your street is. When a civic body defends a price, ask what the agent is paid for before you trust the outcome.

moved.what: Hoteliers say the ₹8-per-litre Nandini milk hike from 1 November will push up coffee, tea and food prices; the hotels association has opposed the increase (The Times of India, Moneycontrol, ThePrint).
moved.so_what: Expect a higher bill for daily tea, coffee and tiffin out from early November. If you eat out daily, set the new figure in your monthly budget now.

moved.what: Railway minister Ashwini Vaishnaw will flag off a Vande Bharat sleeper from Bengaluru to Mumbai on 1 November, a 16-hour journey (The Times of India).
moved.so_what: If you travel to Mumbai, check IRCTC for this service's timings and fares before booking another train or flight.

moved.what: The Pink Line's 7.5-km elevated stretch has safety clearance, and a 15 November opening by PM Modi is reported as likely (Swarajya, Goodreturns).
moved.so_what: Treat 15 November as likely, not confirmed. Do not change a commute or house plan until BMRCL announces public opening.

moved.what: KSRTC and KSTDC have announced 12 tour packages for the Hasanamba Temple festival, while private operators are fully booked (The Hindu).
moved.so_what: If you plan to go, book the KSRTC or KSTDC package now; the private options are gone.

moved.what: The Chief Justice of India expressed shock that people believe they can be arrested over a mobile phone, in a hearing on digital arrest scams (Live Law).
moved.so_what: No agency arrests anyone on a call or video. If someone says you are under arrest on the phone, hang up and call a family member.

carry_over.prompt: ₹8,000 lands in your account and the sender asks you to return it to a different UPI ID than the one it came from: what is the tell?
carry_over.answer: They want the refund to go somewhere other than exactly where it came from.
